reader.decision: Make the four edits now: FROM_ADDRESS, SMTP_RELAY, the retry settings, and hard/soft classification in handle_bounce. Ship them together for the 14 November cutover.
reader.decision_reason: The message lists the exact changes and says it will make them when I say so. Nothing in it blocks the edits, and code edits can be reverted. The block-threshold scope is unclear, so I'll have it confirmed while the work proceeds.

reconstruction.problem: invoice-mailer must move from smtp-old-1 to smtp-mx-2. The cutover date was the last open item, and I set it to 14 November. The config and code still hold the old values. FROM_ADDRESS is billing@larkspur.io, SMTP_RELAY is smtp-old-1.larkspur.internal, and the retry settings are 12 retries at 60-second intervals. handle_bounce cannot tell hard bounces from soft ones.
reconstruction.what_breaks: If the changes don't ship, the 30 November invoice run fails against the offline smtp-old-1. The current 12 retries at 60 seconds would trip the smtp-mx-2 24-hour block on the first bad mailbox. The block threshold is more than 5 bounces per hour (docs/mail-provider.md:3).
reconstruction.fix: Ship four changes together. (1) Set FROM_ADDRESS to invoices@mail.larkspur.io. (2) Set SMTP_RELAY to smtp-mx-2.larkspur.internal. (3) Change the retry settings to at most 3 soft retries per hour. (4) Add hard/soft classification in handle_bounce, calling message.mark_failed() on a hard bounce with no retry. The SPF record already includes smtp-mx-2 (docs/dns.md:6).
reconstruction.cost: Not stated beyond the effort of the four edits. The cutover date leaves 16 days of margin before 30 November.

follow_up_questions: Is the 'more than 5 bounces per hour' threshold counted per recipient, per sender, or for the whole relay? If it is per relay, several bad mailboxes could trip it even with 3 retries each.
Does the 5-per-hour count include the original failed send? If so, one initial bounce plus 3 retries is 4 per mailbox.
reader.closing_answer: Yes, go ahead and make the edits. Ship all four together, and confirm how the smtp-mx-2 block threshold is counted.
